transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks for seeing me. Um… it may sound a little vain, I guess, but I’ve been getting kind of stuck on how my face looks—mostly this sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face. I noticed it a lot after seeing myself in some family photos.

My wife says she barely notices anything, and clients don’t seem to either, so maybe I’m making too much of it… but it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should come talk to someone.
Is it just the appearance of your face that's bothering you?

Yeah, mostly my face. It’s that sagging, kind of uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face that I keep getting hung up on. It really stood out to me after seeing those family photos.

I mean, my wife says she barely sees it, and clients don’t seem to react or anything, so I know it might sound like I’m making too much of it… but that’s the thing I keep coming back to.
Is your concern about your face's appearance always about this sagging, uneven look, or does it vary?

It’s pretty consistently that, yeah—the sagging or unevenness around my jaw and more on one side of my face. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, because like I said, my wife says she barely notices it and clients don’t seem to either. But that’s the thing I keep getting stuck on, especially since those family photos.
How much distress does thinking about your face's appearance cause you?

It’s… more than I’d like to admit, honestly. I mean, I know it probably sounds small, and my wife tells me she barely notices it, and clients don’t seem to either. But when I start thinking about that sagging, uneven look around my jaw—especially on one side—it kind of sticks with me.

It’s not constant panic or anything, but it bothers me enough that it brought me in here. Those family photos really set it off, I think.
Is your concern about your face related to anything other than how it looks?

No, I think it’s really just about how it looks. What brings me in is that I keep getting stuck on that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face… especially after seeing myself in all those family photos.

I know my wife and even clients seem to barely notice anything, so maybe I’m over-focusing on it, but that’s the part I keep coming back to.
Does thinking about the appearance of your face interfere with your daily activities or social interactions?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m still doing what I need to do—I get through my work and I don’t think clients would necessarily know anything is off. But I have noticed I’m slower getting out the door for client meetings, like checking myself or trying to feel okay enough to leave.

And during some appointments I’m probably not as present as I should be, because part of my mind is on whether they’re noticing my face. Socially… I’ve skipped a few art openings, which I usually like, because I just didn’t want to be seen or end up in photos. I know that probably sounds kind of vain, but it has gotten in the way some.
Is your concern about your face's appearance focused on this one issue of sagging and unevenness, or do you find yourself worrying about other flaws as well?

Mostly that one thing, I think. The sagging or unevenness around my jaw, especially one side of my face. That’s the part I keep checking in my head, especially after those family photos.

I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, and maybe I’m just focusing too much on it, since my wife and even clients say they barely notice anything. But no, I wouldn’t say I’m jumping from flaw to flaw—it’s mainly that area that keeps bothering me.
Have you avoided any important life events or activities because of your concerns about your face's appearance?

I wouldn’t say I’ve missed anything really major, thankfully. I mean, I still go to work and handle my responsibilities.

But… I have been slower getting myself out the door for client meetings, and sometimes during appointments I’m not as focused as I should be because I’m thinking about my face. And I’ve skipped a few art openings, which I do normally enjoy, just because I didn’t want to be seen or end up in photos. I know that may not sound like a huge thing, but it’s been happening.
Do you think there's a possibility that your face looks fine and you're just perceiving it differently?

Yeah… I mean, I guess that’s possible. I’m trying to be reasonable about it. My wife says she barely notices anything, and clients haven’t reacted like something is wrong.

But what brings me in is I keep getting stuck on this sagging, uneven look around my jaw—especially one side of my face. It got worse after I saw myself in those family photos. So part of me knows maybe I’m perceiving it more harshly than other people do, but it still feels very noticeable to me.
Do you think other people can see this sagging, uneven look on your face when they look at you?

I think… yes, probably, at least a little. I don’t want to overstate it, because my wife says she barely notices and clients don’t seem to react or anything.

But when I look at myself, especially after seeing those family photos, I get stuck on that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face. So it’s hard for me to believe other people can’t see it too, even if maybe they’re just not saying anything.
Do you think you're ugly when you look at yourself in the mirror?

I don’t usually think, “I’m ugly,” exactly… that feels a little harsh to say. But when I look in the mirror, I do get stuck on my jaw and one side of my face looking kind of saggy or uneven.

And since seeing myself in those family photos, it’s been harder to shake. I know my wife and clients say they barely notice anything, so I’m trying not to make it bigger than it is… but it really stands out to me.
Do you think others find you unattractive because of the sagging, uneven look on your face?

I worry they might, yeah… though I don’t have real proof of that. My wife says she barely notices anything, and clients don’t seem to act like there’s something wrong, so I’m trying not to assume too much.

But what keeps bothering me is that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face—especially since those family photos. It just feels noticeable to me, and then I start wondering if other people are seeing it too and maybe just being polite.
Has your concern about the sagging, uneven look on your face been on your mind for more than an hour a day?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like it’s all day or anything, because I’m still functioning and seeing clients and all that.

But it probably does add up to more than an hour some days. What brings me in is that I keep getting stuck on that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face—especially after seeing myself in those family photos—even though my wife and clients say they barely notice anything. It’s just been hard to let go of once it’s in my head.
Does thinking about the appearance of your face interfere with your ability to enjoy your free time or hobbies?

A little, yeah. I mean, I still get through my work and I don’t want to overstate it, but it has started to affect things.

I’ve noticed I’m slower getting out the door for client meetings because I’m checking how my face looks, and sometimes during appointments I’m not as fully present as I should be. And in my free time… I’ve skipped a few art openings, which I normally enjoy, because I just didn’t want to be seen or end up in photos. Does that make sense?
Does thinking about the sagging, uneven look on your face ever feel like it's intruding into your thoughts, even when you're trying to focus on other things?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t mean it’s constant or that I can’t do anything else, but it does sort of pop back into my mind when I’m trying to focus.

What brings me in is that I keep getting stuck on that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face—especially after seeing it in those family photos. Even though my wife and clients say they barely notice anything, I still find myself thinking about it more than I’d like. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you think your view of your face's appearance is possibly not accurate?

I guess… yes, possibly. I’m not totally sure, because when I look at it, it really does seem obvious to me—the sagging around my jaw and one side looking uneven.

But I also know my wife and even clients have said they barely notice anything, so maybe I’m seeing it more harshly than other people do. That’s part of why I came in, honestly… I keep getting stuck on it, especially after those family photos, and I’m not sure if I’m being reasonable about it.
Do you think your face actually looks saggy and uneven, or is it just that you feel like it should look different?

I think… when I look at it, it does actually look saggy and uneven to me, especially around my jaw and on one side of my face. That’s what I keep getting stuck on.

But I’m also trying to be fair about it, because my wife and even some clients say they barely notice anything. So maybe it’s not as obvious as it feels to me. It just keeps standing out to me, especially after seeing myself in those family photos.
Do you think your face is actually defective in some way, or is it just not perfect?

I don’t know if I’d call it “defective”… that sounds a little strong, and I don’t want to overstate it. But I do keep getting stuck on this sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face.

It’s especially been on my mind since seeing myself in those family photos. I know my wife and even clients say they barely notice anything, so maybe it’s more like it just feels not right to me… or not how it should look. Does that make sense?
Is your concern about your face's appearance limited to the sagging and unevenness, or do you also worry about other aspects of how you look?

Mostly it’s that, yeah—the sagging and the unevenness around my jaw and one side of my face. That’s the thing I keep getting hung up on.

I don’t think I’m sitting around worrying about every part of how I look, at least not in the same way. It’s really been this face thing, especially after those family photos. And I know my wife and clients say they barely notice it, so I feel a little embarrassed even saying it, but that’s what keeps sticking in my mind.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms align with Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD), characterized by a preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance, which are not observable or appear slight to others. The patient's focus on the sagging and unevenness of their face, despite reassurance from others, and the significant distress and impairment it causes in their daily life, support this diagnosis.
